rows.law: A2A agent cards are machine-readable seat introductions; protocol-layer interop is provable independently of application-layer health.
rows.claim: Official Google a2a-sdk 1.1.5 client resolved a live public card (sheyda-a2a-server.hf.space, 533 B, protocolVersion 0.3.0) into the official a2a_pb2.AgentCard proto and completed a JSONRPC send round-trip; the server's executor was broken upstream, which does not negate wire-level interop.
rows.quote:
protocol-layer interop is confirmed live (both sides spoke A2A 0.3.0
JSONRPC correctly); the application layer on that server is broken upstream.
rows.steal: Publish an estate card at /.well-known/agent-card.json so foreign seats can introduce themselves machine-readably, and probe a peer's card before trusting its self-description; grade peers at the protocol layer and the app layer separately.
rows.falsifier: A card the official SDK resolves whose declared transport fails a live send, or a send round-trip that succeeds against a card the resolver rejects.

rows.law: Soft-404 wall: HTTP 200 at a well-known path proves nothing; require content-type application/json plus a JSON parse before calling it a card.
rows.claim: copilot.microsoft.com/.well-known/agent-card.json returned HTTP 200 with ~68 KB of SPA HTML; the official resolver raised AgentCardResolutionError; gemini/anthropic/openai/copilot-api hosts plain 404 at the same path.
rows.quote:
HTTP 200 at the well-known path proves nothing; require
`content-type: application/json` + JSON parse before calling it a card.
rows.steal: Gate every estate endpoint or card probe on content-type plus parse, never status code alone, and file the raw wall bytes as evidence.
rows.falsifier: A 200 text/html well-known response that the official resolver accepts as a card, or a resolver acceptance granted without application/json content-type.

rows.law: Rot probes are alpha-decay meters: separate sentence-death from fact-death; an exact-phrase MISS can be a revision artifact, not a deletion.
rows.claim: photon-aftermath#1's sub-claim that the 20% figure was absent from live bytes is corrected: the 136,746-byte live fetch carries 'approximately 20% fewer equivalent serving machines'; the earlier MISS was exact-phrase only.
rows.quote: The earlier MISS was an exact-phrase artifact of the revision, not a deletion of the claim.
rows.steal: After any exact-phrase MISS, run a key-fact scan over the saved bytes before reporting deletion, and keep both results in the receipt.
rows.falsifier: An exact-phrase MISS where the underlying fact is absent from every saved witness (the 'five months' fragment is the known live instance of true deletion).

rows.law: Verbatim-at-publish requires publication-era bytes; where no archive exists quotes stay permanently stranded, and the stranding itself is a first-class negative finding.
rows.claim: Wayback's entire capture history for the Photon post is one contentless 204 record (replay 403), archive.today has no snapshot, no public mirror found: four stranded quotes are unadjudicable as verbatim-at-publish.
rows.quote: A 204 response has no body by RFC, so this capture holds zero page text: **Wayback still cannot adjudicate the stranded quotes.**
rows.steal: Capture Wayback or archive.today at first contact for any quote intended as load-bearing; treat unarchived vendor prose as unverifiable by default.
rows.falsifier: Surfacing any publication-era capture whose bytes byte-match a currently stranded quote.

rows.law: Mutation vs burn-side fabrication is decidable with independent-time phrasing witnesses: a launch-day mirror carrying the stranded phrasing supports mutation over fabrication.
rows.claim: AlphaSignal's launch-day piece (datePublished 2026-09-24T18:07:51Z, saved 107,585 B) carries '20% fewer machines', matching the stranded quote rather than today's rewording: the first phrasing-level witness for mutation.
rows.quote: carries the stranded phrase "20% fewer machines" that today's post no longer uses verbatim, which is the first phrasing-level witness supporting mutation over burn-side fabrication
rows.steal: Adjudicate quote disputes by fetching and saving launch-day third-party mirrors, then byte-compare against live bytes; keep the HTML so every check re-runs offline.
rows.falsifier: AlphaSignal editing its own text after launch, or a burn-era capture whose bytes match today's live wording instead of the stranded phrasing.
